[1/1] Plan: measure whether any prompt or sampler change beats the accepted code preset on the served sampler, then make a sampler change re-open the prompt it was chosen with

impact_assessment.why: The saved coder profile was screened at temperature 0.7 but serves 0.4; a sampler re-tune leaves the prompt (and its stats) measured on the old sampler, so the applied preset can be unproven under the settings actually used.
impact_assessment.benefits: The saved prompt is always validated on the sampler in use; a sampling-only re-tune marks the prompt pending instead of silently serving an unproven choice.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: tune progress gains sampledWith; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: extra prompt answers after a sampler change; old profiles have no signature and are untouched
impact_assessment.mitigation: paired real-engine screens first, hermetic tune tests for no-op/invalidation/re-measurement, full suite, UI smoke, project gates

Fix: prompt records sampledWith and is re-opened when the sampler changes; tests cover same-sampler no-op, sampling-only invalidation, re-measurement. npm test 590 pass/1 skip; ui:smoke OK; 4/4 gates; checklists: passed

[1/1] Plan: inventory every implicit state machine, verify the findings, judge UX/DX/AX proposals, then land the passing ones behind explicit transition guards

impact_assessment.why: Three subsystems compared status literals inline and the UI kept state in boolean clusters, producing reachable impossible states: a canceled download could be marked complete, a load could stay loading forever, a concurrent start could share a .part, a created API key was erased, and closing Settings discarded edits.
impact_assessment.benefits: One state vocabulary with illegal transitions refused, truthful statuses in the API/UI, persistent restart/auth states, safer polling, and an agent-readable machine catalog at /api/health.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: engine/download/benchmark statuses and /api/health fields; dependency: none; concurrency: start reservation and terminal guards; state: no persisted data migration, legacy profiles untouched
impact_assessment.mitigation: read every cited site, define legal transitions from observed paths, add tests for terminal/race/health/UI states, keep deferred items in docs, run the full suite, UI smoke and project gates

[1/1] Plan: add canonical JSON registries and tests that prove every documented machine location, every passing proposal's code markers and named tests, and the deferred reasons

impact_assessment.why: The prior inventory and proposal documents were prose only; a reviewer could not mechanically confirm that all 25 machines were real, that the proposals were verified, or that the implementation matched the passing ones.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every inventory row names a file and anchor checked by a test; every passing proposal must keep its code markers and named test or the suite fails; deferred proposals must keep a reason.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: docs gain JSON companions; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: tests read the source and documents, fail on drift, and run inside npm test and the project gates

[1/1] Plan: tune Qwen2.5 0.5B on the code task with the fixed harness (device + sampling + prompt), A/B the preset against the gate baseline settings on all 136 code items, and land the measured recipe

impact_assessment.why: The gate model Qwen 0.5B baseline settings score 25.7% on code; a screen showed T=0 plus the suite prompt at 33.3% with fewer tokens, so the tuner had real headroom on a core model.
impact_assessment.benefits: Higher coding score and quality per second/GB on this machine from a measured per-model preset, without touching the baseline.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: user profile and a committed recipe; dependency: local GGUF and Vulkan; concurrency: timing under another benchmark; state: profile overwrite (backup kept)
impact_assessment.mitigation: tune through tune-run.mjs, A/B on identical load/seeds on 136 items, keep a backup, run npm test and tune:gate

[1/1] Plan: test whether a concise answer directive lifts SmolLM2 135M recall, then tune it through the harness and land the measured preset

impact_assessment.why: SmolLM2 recall is a gate model at 6.5% with the suite prompt; a directive screen showed the concise prompt at 13% on the 46-item rung.
impact_assessment.benefits: A measured recall gain on a core gate model without touching the baseline; the tuner picks the prompt with its own paired rule.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: user profile and a committed recipe; dependency: local GGUF on Vulkan; concurrency: other sessions loading the CPU; state: profile overwrite (backup kept)
impact_assessment.mitigation: screen with paired stats, run the tuner prompt stage on a two-candidate grid, confirm on all 65 recall items, run tests and the gate
